title: Preparing trial exhibits on Mac: a guide for paralegals to stop the chaos
metaTitle: Preparing trial exhibits on Mac: guide for paralegals
description: Stop the manual grind of preparing trial exhibits on your Mac. Learn how to organize documents, manage Bates numbering, and reduce administrative burnout.
intro: Preparing trial exhibits is often the most stressful part of a paralegal's day because it requires absolute precision across hundreds of files. When you are managing these documents on a Mac, you need a system that prevents version drift and keeps your evidence ready for court without constant manual intervention.
tldr: Use a single, centralized document management system to avoid file fragmentation.
Automate your Bates numbering process using dedicated Mac-native PDF tools.
Batch your work to reduce context-switching and mental fatigue.
Maintain a master index in Excel to ensure every exhibit is accounted for.
Always follow your firm's specific protocols for handling sensitive client data.

blocks.text: The hidden cost of manual exhibit organization

When you handle exhibit organization manually, you pay a high price in both time and accuracy. Many paralegals spend hours renaming files or manually typing Bates numbers into document footers. This is not just tedious. It creates a massive risk for errors that can derail a trial. If you miss a document or mislabel a page, your team loses credibility in the courtroom.
Why exhibit organization feels like a constant grind

The main cause of this frustration is the lack of a unified workflow. You might receive documents via email, download them to a local folder, and then try to track their status in a separate Excel file. This creates a fragmented environment where the "master" version of an exhibit is hard to find. When you have to switch between Outlook, Finder, and your document management software dozens of times an hour, your focus shatters.
Fixes for better trial exhibit preparation

items: Adopt a standard naming convention immediately. Use a format like YYYY-MM-DD-EXHIBIT-NAME to keep files sorted in Finder.
Use a single master index in Excel or a dedicated case management tool to track every exhibit number.
Automate Bates numbering. Do not add stamps manually. Use tools like Adobe Acrobat Pro or PDF Expert to apply stamps to entire document sets at once.
Batch your work. Spend one hour just renaming files, then one hour just applying stamps. Do not mix tasks.
Clean your desktop daily. Move files into your firm's approved document management system so they are backed up and indexed.

blocks.text: Always verify your firm's specific security policies before moving client files to any cloud service or local tool. Ensure you are compliant with all data privacy requirements.

A simple weekly plan for exhibit management
Consistency is your best defense against exhibit chaos. Follow this simple routine to keep your case files organized without the stress.

faq.question: What is the best way to handle Bates numbering on a Mac?
faq.answer: Use a professional PDF editor like Adobe Acrobat Pro or PDF Expert. These tools allow you to select a folder of documents and apply a consistent Bates stamp to all of them in one operation.

faq.question: How do I keep my exhibit index up to date?
faq.answer: Maintain a master Excel file that is linked to your firm's document management system. Update this index as soon as you add a new document to your exhibit list to avoid backlogs.

faq.question: Can Lazur help me organize my files?
faq.answer: Lazur cannot move files for you, but it can guide you through the steps to organize them. You can ask Lazur where a specific setting is in your file management app, or use it to dictate notes about which documents need to be processed next.

costs.title: Time loss
costs.text: Manual data entry for Bates numbers and file naming steals hours that could be used for substantive legal work.

costs.title: Increased error risk
costs.text: Manual processes lead to missing documents or incorrect numbering, which can damage your firm's case and credibility.

costs.title: Burnout
costs.text: The constant grind of repetitive filing and indexing causes mental fatigue and leads to high turnover in legal support roles.

causes.title: Fragmented workflows
causes.text: Using email, local folders, and spreadsheets separately makes it difficult to track the current status of every exhibit.

causes.title: Lack of automation
causes.text: Relying on manual PDF editing instead of batch processing tools makes simple tasks take three times longer than necessary.

causes.title: Version drift
causes.text: When files are saved in multiple locations, it is easy to lose track of which document is the final, approved version.

fixes.title: Standardize naming
fixes.text: Adopt a firm-wide naming convention for all files so they are always easy to find in Finder or your document management system.

fixes.title: Use batch tools
fixes.text: Use tools like Adobe Acrobat Pro to automate Bates numbering and stamping across hundreds of files at once.

fixes.title: Centralize everything
fixes.text: Stop saving files to your local desktop. Move everything immediately into your firm's approved document management system.

plan.label: Morning
plan.title: Triage and index
plan.text: Spend your first hour reviewing new documents and updating your master Excel index. Do not start any stamping yet.

plan.label: Mid-day
plan.title: Batch processing
plan.text: Use the two hours before lunch to run your Bates numbering and stamping in your PDF tool. This is a high-focus task.

plan.label: End of day
plan.title: Clean up
plan.text: Move all processed files into the final folder and clear your desktop. Ensure no sensitive files remain in your local Downloads folder.
